title: 1966 AHSME Problem 4
statement: Circle \(\mathrm{I}\) is circumscribed about a given square and circle \(\mathrm{II}\) is inscribed in the given square. If \(r\) is the ratio of the area of circle \(\mathrm{I}\) to that of circle \(\mathrm{II},\) then \(r\) equals:

solutions.text:
For square side \(s,\) the outer circle has radius \(\frac{s}{\sqrt2},\) while the inner circle has radius \(\frac{s}{2}.\) Hence \[ r=\frac{\pi(\frac{s}{\sqrt2})^2}{\pi(\frac{s}{2})^2}=2. \]

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: For square side \(s,\) compare radii \(\frac{s}{\sqrt2}\) and \(\frac{s}{2}\)
Circle areas are proportional to the squares of their radii
